data.narrative:
Nuview is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Clint and Katie Graumann that has raised $22.9M to date. The Space & Aerospace sector comprises 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, though same-stage private peers are limited.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression analysis. Using the $22.9M total raised as a value proxy and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to subsequent stage produces an implied valuation of $46M. This method captures expected value creation between funding rounds but carries inherent uncertainty given early-stage risk. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied due to lack of disclosed revenue; while the Space & Aerospace sector median trades at 27.4x PS across six public tickers, private companies rarely disclose sufficient financial data. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable given insufficient comparable-stage peers in the narrow dataset.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $39M to $53M, with $46M as the point estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data, limited private peer visibility at Series A stage, and high volatility in early-stage aerospace valuations. Validation would benefit from founder equity ownership percentages and disclosed burn rates to refine stage-progression assumptions.
